questions.stem:
(a) Explain how Eli failed as a parent. [6 marks]
(b) In what six ways did Israel suffer as a result of Eli's parental irresponsibility? [6 marks]
(c) State three lessons that can be derived from the attitude of Eli. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas were worthless men who did not know the Lord, yet he did not restrain them
2 marks: (a) They took the best of the sacrifices by force before the fat was burnt and lay with women serving at the door of the tent of meeting
2 marks: (a) Eli only mildly rebuked them, honoured his sons above God and ignored God's warnings through the man of God and Samuel
1 mark: (b) Israel was defeated by the Philistines
1 mark: (b) About thirty thousand Israelite foot soldiers were killed
1 mark: (b) The ark of God was captured
1 mark: (b) Hophni and Phinehas, the priests, were killed
1 mark: (b) Eli fell, broke his neck and died; the priesthood of his house was cut off
1 mark: (b) The glory departed from Israel (Ichabod); people lost respect for the offerings of the Lord
1 mark: (c) Parents should discipline and correct their children
1 mark: (c) Leaders must not honour their family above God
1 mark: (c) Sin and indulgence bring punishment on a family and a nation
questions.explanation: Eli's sons abused their priestly office: they seized the best portions of the sacrifices and lay with the women who served at the tent of meeting. Eli heard of it but only gave a mild rebuke, honouring his sons above God, and ignored the warnings of the man of God and of Samuel. As a result Israel was defeated by the Philistines, thirty thousand soldiers died, the ark was captured, Hophni and Phinehas were killed, Eli died on hearing the news, his daughter-in-law named her child Ichabod because the glory had departed, and Eli's house lost the priesthood. Lessons: parents must discipline their children; leaders should put God first; sin brings punishment.

questions.stem:
(a) What circumstances led to the dismissal of Gehazi? [9 marks]
(b) State three lessons that can be learnt from Gehazi's conduct. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Naaman, commander of the Syrian army, was a leper; on the advice of an Israelite maid he came to Elisha to be healed
2 marks: Elisha told him to wash seven times in the Jordan; he did so and was healed
1 mark: Naaman offered Elisha gifts but Elisha refused to take anything
2 marks: Gehazi ran after Naaman and lied that Elisha had sent him to ask for a talent of silver and two festal garments for two sons of the prophets; he hid them in the house
2 marks: When Elisha asked where he had been, Gehazi lied again; Elisha declared that Naaman's leprosy would cling to him and his descendants for ever, and he left a leper
2 marks: Greed/covetousness leads to destruction
2 marks: Lying cannot be hidden from God; dishonesty is punished
2 marks: Servants of God should not commercialise God's gifts; one should be content
questions.explanation: Naaman the Syrian army commander was healed of leprosy after washing seven times in the Jordan as Elisha directed. Elisha refused his gifts, but Gehazi, Elisha's servant, ran after Naaman, falsely claimed that Elisha needed a talent of silver and two changes of clothing for two visiting sons of the prophets, received two talents and hid them. When questioned by Elisha he lied that he had gone nowhere. Elisha, who knew what had happened, pronounced that Naaman's leprosy would cleave to Gehazi and his descendants, and he went out a leper. Lessons: greed brings ruin; lies are exposed; God's gifts should not be sold; contentment is a virtue.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem:
(a)(i) Explain how Nehemiah received the news about the state of affairs in Jerusalem. [3 marks]
(ii) Relate Nehemiah's prayer when he received the news. [6 marks]
(b) Identify three virtues that can be learnt from Nehemiah's reaction. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Nehemiah was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes in the capital Susa
2 marks: (a)(i) Hanani, one of his brethren, and some men from Judah told him that the survivors were in great trouble and shame, the wall of Jerusalem was broken down and its gates burnt
2 marks: (a)(ii) He wept, mourned, fasted and prayed to the great and terrible God who keeps covenant and steadfast love
2 marks: (a)(ii) He confessed the sins of Israel, his father's house and himself, admitting they had not kept the commandments given through Moses
2 marks: (a)(ii) He reminded God of His promise to gather the people if they returned to Him, and asked for success and mercy before the king
2 marks: (b) Patriotism/concern for one's nation
2 marks: (b) Prayerfulness and humility (confession of sin)
2 marks: (b) Courage, compassion and faith in God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes at Susa, received Hanani and men from Judah, who reported that the remnant in Judah was in great trouble and shame and that the wall of Jerusalem was broken and its gates burnt. He sat down, wept, mourned and fasted for days and prayed: he praised God as great and awesome, keeping covenant love; confessed the sins of Israel and of his own family; recalled God's word to Moses that a repentant people would be gathered again; and asked God to grant him mercy before the king. Virtues: patriotism, prayerfulness, humility, faith and courage.

questions.stem:
(a)(i) Outline Jeremiah's message about the sins of Judah. [9 marks]
(ii) State two consequences of such sinfulness. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Judah had forsaken God, the fountain of living waters, and turned to idols/Baal and other gods
2 marks: They trusted in the temple and false prophets who cried 'peace, peace' when there was no peace
2 marks: There was social injustice: oppression of the alien, the fatherless and the widow, shedding of innocent blood, stealing, murder, adultery and swearing falsely
2 marks: They burnt their sons and daughters in the fire and broke the covenant
1 mark: Jeremiah called on them to amend their ways and repent
3 marks: Consequence 1: God would bring an enemy (Babylon) from the north; Jerusalem and the temple would be destroyed
3 marks: Consequence 2: the people would go into exile/captivity and suffer sword, famine and pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah condemned Judah for forsaking the Lord, the fountain of living water, and turning to Baal and other gods; for false confidence in the temple and in prophets who promised peace; for injustice, oppression of widows, orphans and strangers, murder, adultery and false swearing; and for sacrificing their children. He urged them to amend their ways. The consequences were invasion by Babylon from the north, destruction of Jerusalem and the temple, and exile in Babylon with death by sword, famine and pestilence.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) What circumstances led to Jesus' declaration of Himself as the 'Bread of Life'? [9 marks]
(b) Identify three moral lessons in this story. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Jesus had fed the five thousand with five barley loaves and two fish
2 marks: The crowd sought Him across the sea at Capernaum; He told them they sought Him because they ate the loaves, not because of the signs
2 marks: He urged them not to labour for food that perishes but for food that endures to eternal life
2 marks: They asked for a sign, citing the manna their fathers ate in the wilderness; Jesus said it was His Father who gives the true bread from heaven
1 mark: When they asked for this bread, He said 'I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger'
2 marks: Seek spiritual nourishment more than material things
2 marks: Believe in Jesus as the source of eternal life
2 marks: Do not follow Jesus for selfish/material gain
questions.explanation: After feeding the five thousand, Jesus crossed to Capernaum and the crowd followed Him. He told them they sought Him because they had eaten the loaves, and urged them to work for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of man gives. They asked for a sign like the manna Moses gave; Jesus replied that the true bread from heaven is given by His Father. When they asked for that bread, He declared, 'I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst.' Lessons: put spiritual needs first; believe in Christ for eternal life; avoid following Him for material gain.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) Relate Jesus' Sermon on the Mount under the following headings:
(i) Worldly Possession; [6 marks]
(ii) Anxiety. [6 marks]
(b) What three lessons can be learnt from this teaching? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Do not lay up treasures on earth where moth and rust consume and thieves break in, but lay up treasures in heaven
2 marks: (a)(i) Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also; the eye is the lamp of the body
2 marks: (a)(i) No one can serve two masters; you cannot serve God and mammon
2 marks: (a)(ii) Do not be anxious about what to eat, drink or wear; life is more than food and the body more than clothing
2 marks: (a)(ii) God feeds the birds of the air and clothes the lilies of the field, so He will care for His children; anxiety cannot add to one's span of life
2 marks: (a)(ii) Seek first His kingdom and His righteousness and all these things shall be added; do not be anxious about tomorrow
1 mark: (b) Put God first above material things
1 mark: (b) Trust God's providence instead of worrying
1 mark: (b) Avoid greed and materialism
questions.explanation: On possessions Jesus taught that treasures should be stored in heaven, not on earth where they decay or are stolen, because the heart follows one's treasure; the sound eye fills the body with light; and no one can serve both God and mammon. On anxiety He told His hearers not to worry about food, drink or clothing, since God feeds the birds and clothes the lilies and knows their needs; worry adds nothing to life. They should seek first God's kingdom and righteousness and let tomorrow take care of itself. Lessons: put God first, trust His care, avoid materialism.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the Lukan account of the Resurrection. [9 marks]
(b) State three lessons that can be derived from this episode. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: On the first day of the week at early dawn the women went to the tomb with spices they had prepared
2 marks: They found the stone rolled away and did not find the body of the Lord Jesus
2 marks: Two men in dazzling apparel asked why they sought the living among the dead, reminding them that Jesus said He would rise on the third day
2 marks: The women (Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and others) told the apostles, who regarded it as an idle tale
1 mark: Peter ran to the tomb, saw the linen cloths by themselves and went home wondering
2 marks: Jesus has power over death; Christians have hope of resurrection
2 marks: God fulfils His promises
2 marks: Believers should share the good news and not doubt
questions.explanation: Luke records that at early dawn on the first day of the week the women came to the tomb with spices and found the stone rolled away and the body gone. Two men in dazzling clothes appeared and said, 'Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen,' reminding them of His words in Galilee. The women, Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and others, told the eleven, who did not believe them. Peter ran to the tomb, saw the linen cloths lying alone and went home amazed. Lessons: Christ conquered death; God keeps His promises; believers should proclaim the gospel and overcome doubt.

questions.stem:
(a) Trace the events that led to the election of Matthias as one of the twelve. [9 marks]
(b) Highlight three guidelines that should be borne in mind while conducting elections. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, betrayed Jesus and died, leaving his office vacant
2 marks: In the days after the ascension, about 120 believers were gathered and Peter stood up to address them
2 marks: Peter said the scripture had to be fulfilled: 'Let another take his office'; the replacement must have accompanied them from John's baptism to the ascension and be a witness to the resurrection
2 marks: Two were put forward, Joseph called Barsabbas (Justus) and Matthias; they prayed for God to show whom He had chosen
1 mark: They cast lots and the lot fell on Matthias, who was enrolled with the eleven apostles
2 marks: Candidates should be people of good character/qualified for the office
2 marks: Elections should be preceded by prayer and seeking God's will
2 marks: The process should be free, fair and transparent, and the result accepted by all
questions.explanation: After Judas' betrayal and death, Peter addressed about 120 believers, explaining that scripture required someone else to take Judas' office. The person had to be one of those who had been with them throughout Jesus' ministry, from John's baptism to the ascension, so as to witness to the resurrection. Two men, Joseph called Barsabbas (Justus) and Matthias, were nominated; the believers prayed that the Lord, who knows all hearts, would show His choice; they cast lots and the lot fell on Matthias, who was numbered with the eleven. Guidelines: choose qualified people of integrity; pray and seek God's guidance; ensure a fair, transparent process acceptable to all.

questions.stem:
(a) Outline the features of the New Life in Christ as stated by Paul in Colossians. [9 marks]
(b) Identify three practices which can have a negative effect in any Christian community. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Having been raised with Christ, set your minds on things that are above, not on earthly things
2 marks: Put to death immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire and covetousness, which is idolatry
2 marks: Put away anger, wrath, malice, slander, foul talk and lying; put on the new nature, in which there is neither Greek nor Jew, slave nor free
2 marks: Put on compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness and patience, forgiving one another, and above all love
1 mark: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts; be thankful; do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus
2 marks: Immorality/sexual impurity
2 marks: Lying, slander and malice
2 marks: Greed/covetousness, quarrelling, tribalism or discrimination
questions.explanation: Paul taught that those raised with Christ must seek things above. They should put to death fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire and covetousness, and put away anger, wrath, malice, slander, foul talk and lying, having put on the new nature that is renewed in knowledge, where there is no distinction of Greek or Jew, slave or free. They should clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, meekness and patience, forgive one another as the Lord forgave them, and put on love; let Christ's peace rule, let His word dwell richly in them and be thankful. Negative practices: immorality, lying and slander, greed, quarrels and discrimination.

questions.stem:
(a) How did Paul treat the problem of idleness among the Thessalonian Christians? [12 marks]
(b) Give three reasons why Christians should engage in gainful employment. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Some Thessalonians stopped working, thinking the second coming was imminent
2 marks: Paul commanded them in the name of the Lord to keep away from any brother living in idleness
2 marks: He reminded them of his own example: he did not eat anyone's bread without paying but worked night and day so as not to burden them
2 marks: He gave the rule: 'If any one will not work, let him not eat'
2 marks: He rebuked busybodies and charged them to do their work in quietness and earn their own living
2 marks: He urged them not to be weary in well-doing, to note and avoid the disobedient but warn him as a brother
1 mark: To provide for oneself and one's family
1 mark: To avoid being a burden to others
1 mark: To be able to help the needy and support God's work
questions.explanation: Because some believers expected Christ's immediate return, they stopped working and became busybodies. Paul commanded the church to keep away from idle brethren; reminded them that he himself had worked night and day so as not to be a burden, to give them an example; laid down the rule that anyone who will not work should not eat; charged the idle to work quietly and earn their own living; and told the faithful not to grow weary in doing good, to shun the disobedient so he might be ashamed, yet warn him as a brother. Christians should work to support themselves and their families, avoid dependence on others, and be able to give to the needy.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain James' concept of works in relation to Faith. [9 marks]
(b) In what three ways can Christians demonstrate their faith in their daily life? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Faith without works is dead; faith by itself, if it has no works, cannot save
2 marks: Telling a needy brother or sister 'go in peace, be warmed and filled' without giving them what they need is useless
2 marks: Even the demons believe and shudder; mere belief is not enough
2 marks: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; his faith was completed by works; Rahab was justified by works when she received the messengers
1 mark: As the body apart from the spirit is dead, so faith apart from works is dead
2 marks: Caring for the needy, orphans and widows
2 marks: Living a holy life, keeping oneself unstained from the world
2 marks: Honesty, obedience to God's word (being doers and not hearers only), impartiality
questions.explanation: James taught that genuine faith shows itself in action. Faith without works is dead: to wish a hungry, ill-clad brother well without supplying his needs profits nothing. Belief alone is not enough, for even demons believe and tremble. Abraham proved his faith by offering Isaac, and Rahab by hiding the spies; so a man is justified by works and not by faith alone, and as the body without the spirit is dead, so is faith without works. Christians show their faith by helping the needy, being doers of the word, living holy and honest lives and showing no partiality.

questions.stem:
(a) What did Peter teach on interpersonal relationship among Christians? [9 marks]
(b) State three factors which may cause conflict in the society. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Elders should tend the flock of God willingly, not for shameful gain, and not domineering but being examples to the flock
2 marks: Younger ones should be subject to the elders
2 marks: All should clothe themselves with humility toward one another, for God opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble
2 marks: Cast all anxieties on God; be sober and watchful, resisting the devil, firm in faith
1 mark: Love one another earnestly, practise hospitality and serve one another with one's gifts
2 marks: Pride/arrogance and selfishness
2 marks: Injustice, oppression and greed
2 marks: Tribalism/discrimination, lack of love and poor communication
questions.explanation: Peter exhorted elders to shepherd God's flock willingly and eagerly, not for gain nor by domineering but as examples, awaiting the crown of glory from the chief Shepherd. Younger people should submit to the elders, and all should be clothed in humility toward one another, since God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble. They should humble themselves under God's hand, cast their anxieties on Him, be sober and watchful, and resist the devil who prowls like a roaring lion. Conflict in society is caused by pride, selfishness, injustice, greed and discrimination.

questions.stem: In the creation story, the task of giving names to all living creatures was performed by
questions.explanation: God brought the animals to the man to see what he would call them, and whatever he called each creature became its name (Gen. 2:19-20).

questions.stem: God's ability to create by His spoken word depicts His
questions.explanation: Creating all things simply by speaking shows God's unlimited power (omnipotence).

questions.topic: God, the Controller of the universe
questions.stem: God said to Abraham, "To your descendants I shall give this land." Which descendants are referred to here?
questions.explanation: The promise of Canaan was to Abraham's descendants through Isaac and Jacob, the Hebrews (Israelites).

questions.stem: Moses' death was as a result of
questions.explanation: God told Moses he would die without entering Canaan because he broke faith with God at Meribah (Deut. 32:51).

questions.stem: God prepared Joseph for his leadership role in Egypt through
options: the love which his father had for him.
the trials and temptations of his earlier years.
his belief that his dreams would materialise.
the training received from his father.
questions.explanation: Joseph's sale into slavery, temptation by Potiphar's wife and imprisonment shaped him for leadership.

questions.stem: Deborah instructed Barak to engage the forces of Jabin in a battle at
questions.explanation: God said He would draw Sisera, Jabin's general, to Barak at the river Kishon (Judges 4:7).

questions.stem: "The Lord will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman". This statement was directed to
questions.explanation: Deborah told Barak that because he would not go without her, the glory would go to a woman (Judges 4:9).

questions.stem: Who among the following deprived God of the honour due to Him by treating the sacrifices with contempt?
questions.explanation: Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas treated the offering of the Lord with contempt (1 Sam. 2:17).

questions.stem: Prophet Samuel had two worthless sons called
questions.explanation: Samuel's sons Joel and Abijah took bribes and perverted justice (1 Sam. 8:2-3).

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: God's punishment to King Solomon for idolatry was that all
options: his wives and concubines would go to his enemies.
the tribes except Judah would be taken away from him.
his children and wives would go on exile.
the chambers of his palaces would be occupied by his enemies.
questions.explanation: God tore the kingdom from Solomon's house, leaving only one tribe (Judah) for David's sake (1 Kings 11:11-13).

questions.topic: David's submission to the will of God
questions.stem: When David became King of the entire Israel, he moved the capital from
questions.explanation: David reigned at Hebron over Judah, then captured Jerusalem and made it his capital over all Israel.

questions.stem: At Gibeon, God promised to lengthen Solomon's days if he could
questions.explanation: 'If you will walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and commandments... I will lengthen your days' (1 Kings 3:14).

questions.stem: The contest on Mount Carmel was to determine whether
options: the house of Ahab would retain succession to the throne.
Elijah was a true prophet of God.
God or Baal was to be worshipped in Israel.
Jezebel's authority would still prevail in Israel.
questions.explanation: Elijah asked, 'If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him' (1 Kings 18:21).

questions.stem: The prophet that rebuked David for seizing Uriah's wife was
questions.explanation: Nathan rebuked David with the parable of the poor man's ewe lamb (2 Sam. 12).

questions.stem: The king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem because Zedekiah
options: escaped through a breach in the wall.
questions.explanation: Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon, so Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:20-25:1).

questions.stem: The New Covenant was unique because it was
options: written upon the hearts of men.
questions.explanation: Through Jeremiah God promised to put His law within them and write it on their hearts (Jer. 31:33).

questions.stem: The scroll which Ezekiel ate was
questions.explanation: The scroll contained God's words of lamentation, mourning and woe, which Ezekiel was to speak to Israel (Ezek. 2:8-3:4).

questions.stem: The Chaldean officials conspired against Daniel because
options: king Darius had set Daniel over his entire kingdom.
Daniel refused to worship the king's image.
they were jealous of Daniel's wisdom.
Daniel was seen as a foreigner.
questions.explanation: The presidents and satraps plotted against Daniel because the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom (Dan. 6:3-4).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Joseph took Mary but knew her not until she had borne a son because
options: he did not want to disgrace Mary.
he did not want to defile himself.
to do otherwise would defile the child's holiness.
questions.explanation: Joseph did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, took his wife but knew her not until she had borne a son (Matt. 1:24-25).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: According to Jesus in his Sermon on the Mount, "Blessed are the peace makers for
options: "they shall be called sons of God".
questions.explanation: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God' (Matt. 5:9).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Jesus' teaching about discipleship emphasized
options: the need to bury the dead.
a place for the Son of man to lay his head.
putting one's hand unto the plough.
questions.explanation: Jesus demanded that followers put Him above family and comfort and not look back (Luke 9:57-62).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: During the mission of the Twelve, Jesus gave all the following instructions except
options: "go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel".
questions.explanation: He told them to take no gold, silver, bag or spare tunic, for the labourer deserves his food (Matt. 10:9-10).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Which of the following illustrates the parable of the Mustard Seed?
options: The small beginning of Christianity and its universal growth
The full grown mustard tree, attracting different birds to its branches
The gradual development of one's talents
questions.explanation: The smallest of seeds grows into a great tree, showing the kingdom's small beginning and great growth.

questions.stem: The Centurion whose servant Jesus healed demonstrated
questions.explanation: He said he was not worthy for Jesus to enter his house and believed a word would heal; Jesus praised his faith.

questions.stem: As light of the world, Christians are expected to
options: claim that they are born again.
be exemplary in all they do.
questions.explanation: 'Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works' (Matt. 5:16).

questions.stem: In the Transfiguration story, Moses represents the law while Elijah represents the
questions.explanation: Elijah stands for the prophets; together with Moses they show that the Law and the Prophets bear witness to Jesus.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: "As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world." Jesus said this at the
options: raising up of the widow's son.
healing of the man born blind.
questions.explanation: Jesus said this before healing the man born blind (John 9:5).

questions.stem: "This is my beloved son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him". This voice was heard during the
options: baptism of Jesus at River Jordan.
temptation of Jesus in the wilderness.
trial of Jesus before Pontius Pilate.
transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain.
questions.explanation: The words 'listen to him' were added by the voice from the cloud at the Transfiguration (Matt. 17:5).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Jesus performed nature miracles to demonstrate all the following except
questions.explanation: The nature miracles showed His divine power, His concern for people and called for faith; they were not for fame.

questions.stem: Judas Iscariot sealed up his betrayal pact with the chief priests and elders saying "whomsoever I shall
options: dine with, the same is he".
look at, the same is he".
questions.explanation: 'The one I shall kiss is the man; seize him' (Matt. 26:48).

questions.stem: The community of believers in Jerusalem exhibited all the following except
options: continuing daily with one accord in the temple.
praising God and having favour with all people.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:46-47 mentions temple attendance, breaking bread at home and praising God, not marriages.

questions.stem: Peter, in his sermon on the day of Pentecost, called on his audience to
options: receive the power of casting out demons.
receive the power of interpretation of tongues.
questions.explanation: 'Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ' (Acts 2:38).

questions.stem: The disciple in Damascus that God commissioned to restore the sight of Saul was
questions.explanation: Ananias laid hands on Saul and something like scales fell from his eyes (Acts 9:10-18).

questions.stem: "The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men". The statement was made by
questions.explanation: After Paul healed a cripple at Lystra the crowds said this and called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes (Acts 14:11).

questions.stem: Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian cohort in Caesarea, was converted and baptised by
questions.explanation: Peter preached in Cornelius' house and ordered them to be baptized (Acts 10).

questions.stem: Paul made a comparison between Adam and Jesus to show that
options: both Adam and Jesus were human.
Adam succumbed to temptation while Jesus did not.
Adam caused man to sin while Jesus provides salvation.
both were subjected to temptation in the wilderness.
questions.explanation: Through one man sin and death came; through Jesus Christ comes grace and life (Rom. 5:12-19).

questions.stem: The primary motive for Christian offering is to
options: qualify for a mansion in heaven.
respond to God's gift to Christians.
qualify for the pleasures of this world.
questions.explanation: Christian giving is a grateful response to God's inexpressible gift in Christ (2 Cor. 8-9).

questions.stem: Paul warned fathers not to provoke their children because they
questions.explanation: 'Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they become discouraged' (Col. 3:21).

questions.stem: Paul stated that the signs for the Second Coming of Jesus will start with
questions.explanation: 'That day will not come, unless the rebellion comes first' (2 Thess. 2:3).

questions.stem: According to Paul, Grace is a
options: right for all Christians to make wealth.
free gift from God for the man of faith.
questions.explanation: 'By grace you have been saved through faith; it is the gift of God' (Eph. 2:8).

questions.stem: Paul taught that Justification can only be obtained by
questions.explanation: A man is justified by faith in Jesus Christ, not by works of the law (Gal. 2:16; Rom. 3:28).

questions.stem: Paul's letter to Philemon is about
questions.explanation: Paul asked Philemon to forgive and receive back his runaway slave Onesimus as a brother.

questions.stem: Factors that lead to unanswered prayers do not include
questions.explanation: Perseverance helps prayer; sin, doubt and asking wrongly to spend on passions (greed) hinder it.

questions.stem: According to James, effectiveness of prayer depends on
questions.explanation: One must ask in faith with no doubting (James 1:6); the prayer of faith saves the sick (5:15).

questions.stem: An important factor for effective prayer according to James is
questions.explanation: James stresses that prayer offered in faith is effective (James 1:6; 5:15).

questions.stem:
(a) Highlight the covenant promises which God made to Abraham. [9 marks]
(b) In what three ways are these promises significant to Christians? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) God would make of Abraham a great nation and make his name great
2 marks: (a) He would bless those who bless him and curse those who curse him; in him all families of the earth would be blessed
2 marks: (a) His descendants would be as many as the stars of heaven/dust of the earth, though he was old and childless; Sarah would bear a son
2 marks: (a) God would give the land of Canaan to his descendants for ever
1 mark: (a) God would be God to him and his descendants; circumcision was the sign of the covenant
2 marks: (b) Christians, through faith in Christ, are Abraham's offspring and heirs of the promise
2 marks: (b) The blessing of all nations is fulfilled in Jesus Christ, a descendant of Abraham
2 marks: (b) They teach Christians to trust God's faithfulness and to obey Him as Abraham did
questions.explanation: God called Abraham from Haran and promised to make him a great nation, bless him, make his name great, bless those who blessed him and curse those who cursed him, and bless all the families of the earth through him. He promised the land of Canaan to his descendants and that his offspring would be as numerous as the stars, though he and Sarah were old; He would be God to Abraham and his descendants, with circumcision as the sign of the covenant. For Christians, the promise is fulfilled in Christ, through whom all nations are blessed; believers by faith become children of Abraham and heirs; and the story encourages faith and obedience.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the escape of the Israelites from Egypt. [11 marks]
(b) In what two ways was this event significant to Israel? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: After the death of the first-born of Egypt (the Passover), Pharaoh let the Israelites go
2 marks: God led them by a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night by the way of the wilderness towards the Red Sea
2 marks: Pharaoh changed his mind and pursued them with chariots; the people were afraid and complained to Moses
2 marks: Moses told them to fear not but see the salvation of the Lord; at God's command he stretched out his rod and a strong east wind divided the sea
2 marks: The Israelites crossed on dry ground; the Egyptians followed and the waters returned and drowned them
1 mark: Israel saw the great work of the Lord, feared Him and believed in Him and His servant Moses
2 marks: (b) It marked Israel's freedom from slavery and birth as a nation
2 marks: (b) It showed God's power and faithfulness and strengthened their faith; it is remembered in the Passover
questions.explanation: After the tenth plague Pharaoh released the Israelites. God led them by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night towards the Red Sea. Pharaoh regretted letting them go and pursued them with his chariots. The terrified people complained, but Moses assured them that the Lord would fight for them. The angel and the cloud moved between the two camps; Moses stretched his hand over the sea and an east wind drove the waters back, so Israel crossed on dry ground. When the Egyptians followed, the waters returned at Moses' signal and drowned them. Israel feared the Lord and believed in Him and in Moses. The event freed Israel from bondage and made them a nation, and it proved God's power and faithfulness.

questions.topic: David's submission to the will of God
questions.stem:
(a) How did David react to the assassination of Abner? [11 marks]
(b) Indicate two lessons that can be learnt from this incident. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Abner had come to David at Hebron to make a covenant and bring all Israel over to him, and David sent him away in peace
2 marks: Joab, returning, called Abner back and killed him at the gate of Hebron to avenge his brother Asahel
2 marks: David declared that he and his kingdom were for ever guiltless of the blood of Abner and cursed Joab and his house
2 marks: He ordered Joab and all the people to rend their clothes, gird on sackcloth and mourn; David himself followed the bier
2 marks: He wept aloud at the grave, lamented Abner ('Should Abner die as a fool dies?') and refused to eat until sunset
1 mark: He called Abner a prince and a great man and left Joab's punishment to the Lord; the people were pleased and knew he had no part in the murder
2 marks: (b) Revenge/murder is evil and attracts God's judgement
2 marks: (b) Leaders should show sincerity and respect even towards former opponents
questions.explanation: Abner had made peace with David and promised to bring all Israel to him, and David sent him away in peace. Joab returned, privately called Abner back and stabbed him at the gate of Hebron to avenge Asahel. When David heard, he declared himself innocent of Abner's blood and pronounced a curse on Joab's house. He commanded Joab and all the people to tear their clothes, wear sackcloth and mourn; he walked behind the bier, wept at the tomb, composed a lament, fasted till evening and publicly honoured Abner as a great prince. The people were pleased and knew David had not ordered the killing. Lessons: revenge and bloodshed are wrong; leaders should be sincere and magnanimous towards opponents.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how the faith of Shedrach, Meshach and Abednego was tested in Babylon. [11 marks]
(b) Give four examples of cultural practices which are contrary to the Christian faith in your society. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image on the plain of Dura and commanded all officials to fall down and worship it at the sound of music
2 marks: Anyone who refused would be cast into a burning fiery furnace
2 marks: Certain Chaldeans accused Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego of not serving the king's gods or worshipping the image
2 marks: They told the furious king that their God was able to deliver them, but even if not, they would not worship the image
2 marks: The furnace was heated seven times more; they were bound and thrown in, and the men who threw them were killed by the flames
1 mark: The king saw four men walking unhurt in the fire; they came out unharmed and the king praised their God and promoted them
1 mark: (b) Idol/ancestor worship and sacrifices to deities
1 mark: (b) Consulting oracles, diviners and charms
1 mark: (b) Widowhood rites that are dehumanising
1 mark: (b) Female genital mutilation, killing of twins or other harmful practices; secret cults
questions.explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden image and ordered everyone to worship it when the music sounded, on pain of being thrown into a blazing furnace. Chaldeans reported that the three Jews refused. Before the enraged king they declared that their God could deliver them, and that even if He did not, they would not serve his gods. The furnace was heated seven times hotter; they were bound and thrown in, and the soldiers who carried them died from the heat. The king then saw four men walking free in the fire, the fourth like a son of the gods; the three came out unhurt, and the king blessed their God and promoted them. Contrary cultural practices include idol worship, divination and charms, harmful widowhood rites, and practices such as genital mutilation or secret cults.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of Mary's encounter with Angel Gabriel. [11 marks]
(b) State two significant points in Mary's reply to the angel's announcement. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: In the sixth month (of Elizabeth's pregnancy) God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth to a virgin betrothed to Joseph, of the house of David, named Mary
2 marks: He greeted her: 'Hail, O favoured one, the Lord is with you'; she was troubled at the saying
2 marks: He told her not to fear: she would conceive and bear a son and call his name Jesus; He would be great, called Son of the Most High, and reign over the house of Jacob for ever
2 marks: Mary asked how this could be since she had no husband
2 marks: Gabriel said the Holy Spirit would come upon her and the power of the Most High overshadow her, so the child would be called holy, the Son of God; Elizabeth had also conceived in old age, for with God nothing is impossible
1 mark: Mary answered, 'Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word', and the angel departed
2 marks: (b) Humility and willing submission to God's will ('handmaid of the Lord')
2 marks: (b) Faith/trust in God's word that nothing is impossible with God
questions.explanation: In the sixth month God sent Gabriel to Nazareth to Mary, a virgin betrothed to Joseph of David's house. He greeted her as highly favoured; when she was troubled he told her not to fear, for she would conceive and bear a son named Jesus, who would be great, the Son of the Most High, and would reign on David's throne for ever. Mary asked how, since she knew no man. Gabriel replied that the Holy Spirit would come upon her, so the child would be called holy, the Son of God, and that her kinswoman Elizabeth had conceived in her old age, for nothing is impossible with God. Mary replied, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.' Her reply shows humility, obedience and faith.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the roles of Joseph of Arimathea and the women in the burial of Jesus. [9 marks]
(b) In what three ways was Joseph's action significant? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council and a secret disciple who was looking for the kingdom of God, went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus
2 marks: Pilate, after confirming from the centurion that Jesus was dead, granted the body to Joseph
2 marks: Joseph bought a linen shroud, took down the body, wrapped it and laid it in his own new tomb hewn out of rock, and rolled a stone against the door
2 marks: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses (the women from Galilee) followed and saw the tomb and how the body was laid
1 mark: The women went home and prepared spices and ointments to anoint the body after the Sabbath
2 marks: (b) It showed courage in identifying with Jesus at a dangerous time
2 marks: (b) It ensured a decent burial and fulfilled the prophecy that He would be with the rich in His death
2 marks: (b) It confirmed the reality of Jesus' death and provided the known tomb that was later found empty
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who awaited God's kingdom and had not consented to the council's decision, took courage, went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. Pilate, surprised that Jesus was already dead, confirmed it with the centurion and released the body. Joseph bought linen, took the body down, wrapped it and laid it in his own new rock tomb, rolling a stone over the entrance. The women from Galilee, including Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses, watched where He was laid, then went to prepare spices to anoint Him after the Sabbath. Joseph's act showed courage and devotion, gave Jesus an honourable burial in fulfilment of scripture, and established the fact of His death and the empty tomb.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the event that portrayed Jesus as the "Resurrection and the life". [11 marks]
(b) What two lessons can be drawn from this declaration? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha, fell ill and his sisters sent word to Jesus; Jesus delayed two days, saying the illness was for God's glory
2 marks: When Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb four days; Martha met Him and said if He had been there her brother would not have died
2 marks: Jesus said, 'I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live'; Martha confessed Him as the Christ, the Son of God
2 marks: Mary came weeping with the Jews; Jesus was deeply moved and wept, and went to the tomb
2 marks: He ordered the stone removed, prayed to the Father, and cried with a loud voice, 'Lazarus, come out'
1 mark: Lazarus came out bound in grave cloths; Jesus said 'Unbind him, and let him go', and many Jews believed
2 marks: (b) Jesus has power over death and gives eternal life to believers
2 marks: (b) Faith in Jesus is necessary; Christians need not despair at death
questions.explanation: Lazarus of Bethany fell ill and his sisters sent for Jesus, who stayed two more days, saying the sickness was for God's glory. When He came, Lazarus had been buried four days. Martha told Him her brother would not have died had He been present; Jesus assured her he would rise and declared, 'I am the resurrection and the life'; she confessed Him as Christ. Seeing Mary and the Jews weeping, Jesus wept. At the tomb He ordered the stone removed, thanked the Father and cried, 'Lazarus, come out.' The dead man came out bound in grave clothes and Jesus had him released; many believed. Lessons: Jesus conquers death and gives eternal life; believers should have faith and hope in the face of death.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how Herod opposed the early church. [11 marks]
(b) Identify two consequences of this opposition. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: King Herod laid violent hands on some who belonged to the church
2 marks: He killed James the brother of John with the sword
2 marks: Seeing that it pleased the Jews, he arrested Peter during the days of Unleavened Bread, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover
2 marks: Peter was kept in prison guarded by four squads of soldiers, chained between two soldiers; the church prayed earnestly for him
2 marks: An angel released Peter; Herod searched for him, examined the sentries and ordered them to be put to death
1 mark: Herod was later struck down by an angel of the Lord at Caesarea and eaten by worms because he did not give God the glory
2 marks: (b) The church lost James, its first apostle martyr, but grew in prayer and unity
2 marks: (b) The word of God grew and multiplied; Herod himself died a shameful death
questions.explanation: About that time King Herod (Agrippa I) began to persecute the church. He executed James the brother of John with the sword, and when he saw that this pleased the Jews he arrested Peter during the feast of Unleavened Bread, planning to try him publicly after the Passover. Peter was guarded by four squads of soldiers, but the church prayed earnestly and an angel led him out of prison. Herod searched for him in vain and had the guards executed. Later, at Caesarea, Herod accepted the people's acclamation that his was the voice of a god, and an angel struck him down; he was eaten by worms and died. Consequences: the church lost James but grew stronger in prayer, and the word of God spread and multiplied.

questions.stem:
(a) Outline Paul's message on justification. [11 marks]
(b) State two conditions for the attainment of justification. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; no one is justified by works of the law
2 marks: Justification is a free gift of God's grace through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus
2 marks: God put forward Christ as an expiation by His blood, to be received by faith
2 marks: Abraham was justified by faith before circumcision; his faith was reckoned to him as righteousness
2 marks: Justified by faith, we have peace with God; while we were yet sinners Christ died for us
1 mark: As sin came through Adam, so justification and life come through Christ
2 marks: (b) Faith in Jesus Christ
2 marks: (b) Repentance from sin and acceptance of God's grace
questions.explanation: Paul taught that all, Jews and Gentiles, have sinned and fall short of God's glory, and that no human being is justified by works of the law. Righteousness comes as God's free gift through faith in Jesus Christ, whom God put forward as a sacrifice of atonement by His blood. Abraham was reckoned righteous through faith even before circumcision, so he is father of all who believe. Being justified by faith we have peace with God, since Christ died for us while we were still sinners. As one man's (Adam's) sin brought condemnation, one man's (Christ's) obedience brings justification and life. Conditions: faith in Christ and repentance, accepting God's grace.

questions.stem:
(a) According to Paul, what are the signs of the parousia? [12 marks]
(b) State three lessons relevant to Christians in Paul's explanation. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: The day of the Lord will not come unless the rebellion (apostasy) comes first
2 marks: The man of lawlessness, the son of perdition, will be revealed
2 marks: He will oppose and exalt himself against every so-called god, take his seat in the temple of God and proclaim himself to be God
2 marks: His coming will be by the activity of Satan, with pretended signs and wonders and wicked deception of those who are perishing
2 marks: The mystery of lawlessness is already at work but is restrained until the restrainer is removed
2 marks: The Lord Jesus will slay him with the breath of His mouth and destroy him by His appearing; the Lord will descend with a cry of command and the trumpet of God
1 mark: (b) Christians should not be easily shaken or deceived by false teachers
1 mark: (b) They should stand firm and hold to the traditions/teaching they received
1 mark: (b) They should be watchful, live holy lives and continue working
questions.explanation: Paul told the Thessalonians not to be alarmed by claims that the day of the Lord had come. First the rebellion must come and the man of lawlessness be revealed; he will oppose every god, exalt himself, sit in God's temple and proclaim himself God. His coming will be by Satan's power with false signs and wonders that deceive those perishing. The mystery of lawlessness is already at work but is held back by a restrainer; when it is removed the lawless one will appear, and the Lord Jesus will destroy him by the breath of His mouth and the splendour of His coming, descending from heaven with the trumpet of God. Lessons: do not be deceived, stand firm in sound teaching, stay watchful, holy and diligent.

questions.stem:
(a) How did Paul convince the Galatians that Christians are children of God? [11 marks]
(b) Indicate two ways Christians should manifest themselves as children of God. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: In Christ Jesus all are sons of God through faith; those baptized into Christ have put on Christ
2 marks: There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female; all are one in Christ Jesus
2 marks: If you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise
2 marks: An heir, while a child, is no better than a slave, under guardians; so we were slaves to the elemental spirits of the universe
2 marks: When the time had fully come, God sent forth His Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those under the law so that we might receive adoption as sons
1 mark: Because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts crying 'Abba! Father!'; so you are no longer a slave but a son and heir
2 marks: (b) By living by the Spirit and showing the fruit of the Spirit (love, joy, peace, etc.)
2 marks: (b) By loving one another, avoiding the works of the flesh and obeying God
questions.explanation: Paul argued that through faith in Christ believers become sons of God; baptized into Christ, they have put on Christ, and in Him distinctions of Jew and Greek, slave and free, male and female disappear. Belonging to Christ makes them Abraham's offspring and heirs of the promise. Before Christ, people were like minor heirs under guardians, enslaved to the elemental spirits; but in the fullness of time God sent His Son, born of a woman under the law, to redeem those under the law so they might be adopted as sons. As proof, God sent the Spirit of His Son into their hearts crying 'Abba, Father'. Christians show they are God's children by walking in the Spirit, bearing its fruit and loving one another.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain Peter's description of Christians as "a Chosen Race and a Royal Priesthood".... [11 marks]
(b) Give two examples in a Christian's daily life to support the above description. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Christians are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people
2 marks: They were chosen to declare the wonderful deeds of Him who called them out of darkness into His marvellous light
2 marks: Once they were no people but now they are God's people; once they had not received mercy but now they have
2 marks: As living stones they are built into a spiritual house to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ
2 marks: As aliens and exiles they must abstain from the passions of the flesh
1 mark: They must maintain good conduct among the Gentiles so that those who speak against them may see their good deeds and glorify God
2 marks: (b) Living a holy life and avoiding immorality
2 marks: (b) Evangelism, prayer and good deeds/service in the community
questions.explanation: Peter told believers that they are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation and God's own people, called out of darkness into His marvellous light so that they may proclaim His mighty acts. Formerly they were not a people and had not received mercy; now they are God's people and have received mercy. Like living stones they form a spiritual house and a holy priesthood offering spiritual sacrifices through Christ. As strangers and exiles they must abstain from fleshly desires and live honourably among the Gentiles, so that their good works lead others to glorify God. In daily life Christians show this by holy living, prayer and worship, witnessing and doing good to others.

questions.explanation: God would punish the house of Jehu for the blood of Jezreel, where Jehu massacred Ahab's house (Hos. 1:4).

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of Joseph's first encounter with Pharaoh. [12 marks]
(b) State any three qualities of his that earned him Pharaoh's favour. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Pharaoh dreamt of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows, and of seven full ears of grain swallowed by seven thin ears; none of his magicians or wise men could interpret them
2 marks: The chief butler remembered Joseph, who had correctly interpreted his dream in prison, and told Pharaoh
2 marks: Pharaoh sent for Joseph; he was brought out of the dungeon, shaved, changed his clothes and came before Pharaoh
2 marks: Joseph said, 'It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh a favourable answer', and Pharaoh related his dreams
2 marks: Joseph explained that the two dreams were one: seven years of plenty would be followed by seven years of famine
2 marks: He advised Pharaoh to appoint a discerning and wise man and overseers to store a fifth of the produce in the good years against the famine; Pharaoh set Joseph over all Egypt
1 mark: (b) Humility and faith in God (he gave God the credit)
1 mark: (b) Wisdom/discernment and the gift of interpreting dreams
1 mark: (b) Honesty, foresight and good counsel/administrative ability
questions.explanation: Pharaoh had two dreams: seven fat cows devoured by seven gaunt cows, and seven plump ears of grain swallowed by seven thin ears. His magicians could not interpret them. The chief butler then remembered Joseph, who had interpreted his dream in prison. Joseph was hurriedly brought from the dungeon, shaved and changed. He told Pharaoh that interpretation belonged to God, then explained that both dreams meant seven years of great plenty followed by seven years of severe famine, repeated because God had fixed it. He advised Pharaoh to appoint a wise man with overseers to collect a fifth of the harvest in the good years and store it. Pharaoh, impressed, made Joseph ruler over Egypt. Joseph's humility, God-given wisdom and practical foresight won Pharaoh's favour.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the story of the death of the first child born to David by Uriah's wife. [9 marks]
(b) State any three lessons to be derived from the episode. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: After Nathan rebuked David over Uriah and Bathsheba, he said that because David had scorned the Lord, the child born to him would die
2 marks: The Lord struck the child and it became sick; David besought God, fasted and lay all night on the ground
2 marks: The elders of his house could not raise him or make him eat; on the seventh day the child died and the servants feared to tell him
2 marks: Perceiving their whispering, David learnt the child was dead; he arose, washed, anointed himself, changed his clothes, worshipped in the house of the Lord and then ate
1 mark: He explained that while the child lived he fasted hoping God might be gracious, but now he could not bring him back: 'I shall go to him, but he will not return to me'
2 marks: (b) Sin has consequences even when forgiven
2 marks: (b) One should accept God's will/judgement humbly
2 marks: (b) Prayer and fasting are proper responses in times of trouble; there is hope after death
questions.explanation: When Nathan exposed David's sin with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah, David confessed and was forgiven, but Nathan declared that the child born to him would die. The child fell seriously ill. David pleaded with God, fasted and lay on the ground all night, refusing food from his elders. On the seventh day the child died; the servants were afraid to tell him, but David guessed from their whispering. He then got up, washed, anointed himself, changed his clothes, worshipped in the house of the Lord and ate. To his puzzled servants he explained that he had fasted while there was hope, but now the child could not return; he would go to him. Later Bathsheba bore Solomon. Lessons: sin brings consequences; accept God's will; turn to God in prayer in distress.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe Saul's battle with the Philistines on Mount Gilboa. [11 marks]
(b) Give two reasons why the outcome of this battle could be blamed on Saul. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: The Philistines fought against Israel and the men of Israel fled and fell slain on Mount Gilboa
2 marks: The Philistines overtook Saul and his sons and killed Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchishua
2 marks: The battle pressed hard on Saul; the archers found him and he was badly wounded
2 marks: Saul asked his armour-bearer to kill him lest the uncircumcised abuse him; the armour-bearer refused, so Saul fell on his own sword and the armour-bearer did likewise
2 marks: The Israelites in the valley and beyond the Jordan fled and the Philistines occupied their cities
1 mark: The Philistines cut off Saul's head, put his armour in the temple of Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan; the men of Jabesh-gilead rescued and buried the bodies
2 marks: (b) Saul had disobeyed God (e.g. sparing Agag and the best of Amalek), so God's Spirit left him
2 marks: (b) He consulted a medium instead of God, and lacked divine guidance
questions.explanation: The Philistines attacked Israel on Mount Gilboa; Israel fled and many were slain. The Philistines pursued Saul and killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchishua. Saul was badly wounded by archers and begged his armour-bearer to kill him so that the uncircumcised would not abuse him. When the armour-bearer refused, Saul fell on his own sword, and the armour-bearer did the same. The Israelites abandoned their cities, which the Philistines occupied. Next day the Philistines cut off Saul's head, hung his armour in the temple of Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan, until the valiant men of Jabesh-gilead took the bodies and buried them. Saul was to blame because his disobedience made God reject him, and he turned to a medium rather than to God.

questions.stem:
(a) Relate the experience of Jonah as he fled from the presence of God to Tarshish. [11 marks]
(b) Give two moral lessons that could be learnt from his flight. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh and cry against it, but he went down to Joppa and took a ship to Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord
2 marks: The Lord sent a great wind and a mighty tempest; the mariners were afraid, cried to their gods and threw the cargo overboard
2 marks: Jonah was fast asleep in the inner part of the ship; the captain woke him and told him to call on his God
2 marks: They cast lots and the lot fell on Jonah; he confessed he was a Hebrew who feared the Lord and was fleeing from Him
2 marks: He told them to throw him into the sea; after trying to row to land, they prayed and threw him in, and the sea ceased raging
1 mark: The Lord appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah; he was in its belly three days and three nights, prayed, and was vomited onto dry land
2 marks: (b) No one can run away from God/escape His presence
2 marks: (b) Disobedience brings trouble on oneself and others; one should obey God's call promptly
questions.explanation: God commanded Jonah to go and preach against Nineveh, but Jonah fled to Joppa and boarded a ship for Tarshish. The Lord hurled a great storm on the sea; the frightened sailors prayed to their gods and lightened the ship, while Jonah slept below until the captain woke him. They cast lots to find who caused the trouble, and the lot fell on Jonah, who confessed that he worshipped the Lord, maker of sea and land, and was fleeing from Him. He told them to throw him overboard; after vainly rowing for shore they prayed for mercy and threw him in, and the sea became calm. The sailors feared the Lord. A great fish swallowed Jonah; after three days and nights of prayer he was vomited onto land. Lessons: one cannot hide from God; disobedience brings suffering to self and others, so obey God promptly.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) Explain Luke's account of the healing of the Demoniac. [13 marks]
(b) Give two reasons why the evil spirits were sent into the swine. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Jesus arrived in the country of the Gerasenes, opposite Galilee; a man from the city who had demons met Him
2 marks: For a long time he had worn no clothes and lived among the tombs; though bound with chains he broke them and was driven into the desert
2 marks: He fell before Jesus and cried, 'What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beseech you, do not torment me'
2 marks: Asked his name, he said 'Legion', for many demons had entered him; they begged not to be sent into the abyss
2 marks: They begged to enter a large herd of swine feeding on the hillside; Jesus permitted them and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned
2 marks: The herdsmen told it in the city and country; people came and found the man clothed and in his right mind, sitting at Jesus' feet, and were afraid and asked Jesus to leave
1 mark: The man begged to go with Jesus, but Jesus sent him home to declare how much God had done for him
1 mark: (b) To show the man and others that the demons had truly left him
1 mark: (b) Because the demons begged not to be sent into the abyss, and to show the destructive nature of evil spirits
questions.explanation: When Jesus landed in the country of the Gerasenes, He was met by a man possessed by demons who had long gone naked, lived in the tombs, and broke the chains used to bind him. He fell before Jesus crying, 'What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Do not torment me.' He gave his name as Legion because many demons had entered him. The demons begged not to be sent into the abyss but into a large herd of swine; Jesus allowed it, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned. The herdsmen reported it; the people came, found the man clothed and sane at Jesus' feet, and fearfully asked Jesus to leave. The healed man wished to follow Jesus but was sent home to tell what God had done. The spirits were sent into the swine because they pleaded not to go into the abyss, and so that all could see the man had truly been delivered.

questions.stem:
(a) Outline the parables of the lost sheep and the lost coin. [11 marks]
(b) In what two ways are these parables significant? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Tax collectors and sinners drew near to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees and scribes murmured that He received sinners and ate with them
2 marks: Lost sheep: a man with a hundred sheep who loses one leaves the ninety-nine in the wilderness and goes after the lost one until he finds it
2 marks: He lays it on his shoulders rejoicing, calls his friends and neighbours to rejoice with him; so there is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous
2 marks: Lost coin: a woman with ten silver coins who loses one lights a lamp, sweeps the house and seeks diligently until she finds it
2 marks: She calls her friends and neighbours to rejoice with her for finding the coin
1 mark: Likewise there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents
2 marks: (b) God loves sinners and actively seeks the lost
2 marks: (b) Heaven rejoices over repentance; Christians should welcome and seek out sinners
questions.explanation: When the Pharisees and scribes grumbled that Jesus welcomed sinners and ate with them, He told two parables. A shepherd with a hundred sheep who loses one leaves the ninety-nine and searches until he finds it, carries it home on his shoulders and invites friends to rejoice; so there is more joy in heaven over one repentant sinner than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance. A woman with ten silver coins who loses one lights a lamp, sweeps the house and searches carefully until she finds it, then calls her friends to rejoice; likewise there is joy before God's angels over one sinner who repents. The parables show God's seeking love for sinners and the joy of heaven over repentance, and they challenge believers to seek and welcome the lost.

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of the trial of Jesus before the high priest. [9 marks]
(b) Describe Peter's behaviour during this period. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Jesus was led to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered; the chief priests and council sought false testimony to put Him to death
2 marks: Many false witnesses came but their testimony did not agree; at last two said He claimed He could destroy the temple and build it in three days
2 marks: Jesus kept silent; the high priest adjured Him by the living God to say if He was the Christ, the Son of God
2 marks: Jesus answered, 'You have said so', and that they would see the Son of man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds
1 mark: The high priest tore his robes and declared it blasphemy; they judged Him deserving death, spat on Him, struck Him and mocked Him
2 marks: (b) Peter followed at a distance into the courtyard and sat with the guards to see the end
2 marks: (b) A maid said he was with Jesus; he denied it; another maid said the same and he denied with an oath; bystanders recognised his accent and he cursed and swore he did not know the man
2 marks: (b) Immediately the cock crowed; Peter remembered Jesus' words, went out and wept bitterly
questions.explanation: After His arrest Jesus was taken to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the council sought false evidence to have Him killed. Many false witnesses contradicted one another until two claimed He said He would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days. Jesus remained silent. The high priest then put Him on oath to say whether He was the Christ, the Son of God. Jesus replied, 'You have said so,' adding that they would see the Son of man at the right hand of Power coming on the clouds. The high priest tore his robes and cried blasphemy; the council condemned Him to death, spat on Him and struck Him. Meanwhile Peter, who had followed at a distance, sat in the courtyard. Challenged by a maid, then another, and then the bystanders, he denied Jesus three times, finally with curses and oaths. The cock crowed, Peter remembered Jesus' prediction, went out and wept bitterly.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the story of how Lazarus was raised from death. [11 marks]
(b) Give two lessons which the story teaches christians. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, was ill; the sisters sent to Jesus, who said the illness was for the glory of God and stayed two more days
2 marks: Jesus told the disciples Lazarus had fallen asleep (died) and went to Judea; on arrival Lazarus had been in the tomb four days
2 marks: Martha met Jesus; He said, 'I am the resurrection and the life'; she confessed Him as the Christ, the Son of God
2 marks: Mary and the mourning Jews came; Jesus was deeply moved and wept, and went to the tomb, a cave with a stone
2 marks: He ordered the stone taken away despite Martha's objection, lifted His eyes and thanked the Father
1 mark: He cried 'Lazarus, come out'; the dead man came out bound with bandages and Jesus said 'Unbind him and let him go'
2 marks: (b) Jesus has power over death; believers will rise again
2 marks: (b) Faith in Jesus brings God's glory; Jesus shares in human sorrow
questions.explanation: Lazarus of Bethany fell sick, and his sisters Martha and Mary sent word to Jesus. He said the illness was for God's glory and delayed two days, then went to Judea, telling the disciples that Lazarus was dead. When He arrived, Lazarus had been buried four days. Martha met Him, and He declared, 'I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live'; she confessed Him as the Christ. Seeing Mary and the Jews weeping, Jesus wept. At the tomb He ordered the stone removed, thanked the Father for hearing Him, and cried with a loud voice, 'Lazarus, come out.' Lazarus came out still wrapped in grave cloths, and Jesus ordered him unbound. Many believed. Lessons: Jesus has power over death and gives eternal life; faith in Him reveals God's glory; He sympathises with human grief.

questions.stem:
(a) With reference to Paul's epistle to the Philippians, explain how Jesus demonstrated humility. [11 marks]
(b) Mention two ways one can exhibit this virtue. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Paul urged the Philippians to have the mind which was in Christ Jesus, doing nothing from selfishness or conceit but counting others better than themselves
2 marks: Though He was in the form of God, He did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped
2 marks: He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant
2 marks: He was born in the likeness of men and was found in human form
2 marks: He humbled Himself and became obedient unto death, even death on a cross
1 mark: Therefore God highly exalted Him and gave Him the name above every name, that every knee should bow and every tongue confess Him as Lord
2 marks: (b) Serving others and putting their interests before one's own
2 marks: (b) Avoiding pride/boasting and respecting everyone, including those of lower status
questions.explanation: Paul told the Philippians to look to the interests of others and to have the same mind that was in Christ Jesus. Although Christ was in the form of God, He did not cling to equality with God but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant and being born in human likeness. Being found in human form, He humbled Himself further by becoming obedient to death, even death on a cross. Because of this God highly exalted Him and gave Him the name above every name, so that every knee should bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. Christians show humility by serving others, putting others' interests first and avoiding pride and self-seeking.

questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission to the Gentiles
questions.stem: Outline Paul's teaching on spiritual gifts. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: No one speaking by the Spirit of God says 'Jesus be cursed', and no one can say 'Jesus is Lord' except by the Holy Spirit
2 marks: There are varieties of gifts but the same Spirit, varieties of service but the same Lord, varieties of working but the same God
2 marks: To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good
3 marks: The gifts include the utterance of wisdom, utterance of knowledge, faith, gifts of healing, working of miracles, prophecy, ability to distinguish spirits, various kinds of tongues and interpretation of tongues
2 marks: All are inspired by one Spirit, who apportions to each one individually as He wills
2 marks: The church is like one body with many members; every member is needed and none should despise another
2 marks: Christians should earnestly desire the higher gifts, but love is the more excellent way; gifts should be used in order to edify the church
questions.explanation: Paul taught the Corinthians that confessing 'Jesus is Lord' is possible only by the Holy Spirit. There are different gifts, services and workings, but the same Spirit, Lord and God inspires them all, and each manifestation is given for the common good. The gifts include wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discernment of spirits, tongues and interpretation of tongues, distributed by the one Spirit as He wills. Like the parts of a human body, each member of the church has a role; none should feel inferior or superior, and all should care for one another. Believers should desire the higher gifts, especially prophecy, but love is the more excellent way, and all gifts must be exercised decently and in order to build up the church.

questions.stem:
(a) Highlight how James proved that "faith apart from work is dead." [11 marks]
(b) Mention two deeds of faith. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: What does it profit if a man says he has faith but has not works? Can his faith save him?
2 marks: If a brother or sister is ill-clad and lacks food and one says 'Go in peace, be warmed and filled' without giving them what they need, it profits nothing
2 marks: Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead; 'show me your faith apart from works and I by my works will show you my faith'
2 marks: Even the demons believe that God is one, and shudder
2 marks: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac on the altar; his faith was completed by works; Rahab was justified by works when she received the messengers
1 mark: As the body apart from the spirit is dead, so faith apart from works is dead
2 marks: (b) Feeding, clothing and caring for the poor, orphans and widows
2 marks: (b) Obedience to God's word even at a cost (e.g. Abraham offering Isaac, Rahab protecting the spies)
questions.explanation: James argued that faith without works cannot save. Wishing a hungry and poorly clothed brother well without meeting his needs is useless; such faith is dead. Anyone can claim faith, but true faith is shown by works. Mere belief is not enough, for even demons believe in one God and tremble. Abraham's faith was proved and completed when he offered Isaac, and he was called God's friend; Rahab the harlot was justified by works when she welcomed and hid the spies. So a person is justified by works and not by faith alone; as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead. Deeds of faith include caring for the poor, widows and orphans and obeying God even at personal cost.

questions.stem:
(a) Relate the teaching of James on effective prayer. [11 marks]
(b) Give four causes of unanswered prayers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: If any one lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all men generously and without reproaching
2 marks: He must ask in faith, with no doubting; the doubter is like a wave of the sea driven by the wind and should not expect anything from the Lord
2 marks: Is any one suffering? Let him pray; is any cheerful? Let him sing praise
2 marks: Is any sick? Let him call the elders of the church to pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; the prayer of faith will save the sick and his sins will be forgiven
2 marks: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another; the prayer of a righteous man has great power in its effects
1 mark: Elijah, a man of like nature with us, prayed that it might not rain and it did not rain for three years and six months; he prayed again and the heaven gave rain
1 mark: (b) Doubt/lack of faith
1 mark: (b) Unconfessed sin
1 mark: (b) Asking with wrong motives (to spend on one's passions)
1 mark: (b) Unforgiveness/broken relationships or not being persistent
questions.explanation: James taught that anyone lacking wisdom should ask God, who gives generously, but must ask in faith without doubting, for the doubter is unstable like a wave tossed by the wind. The suffering should pray and the cheerful should sing praises. The sick should call the elders of the church to pray over them and anoint them with oil; the prayer of faith will heal the sick, and any sins will be forgiven. Believers should confess their sins to one another and pray for one another, for the prayer of a righteous person is powerful. Elijah, an ordinary man, prayed and it did not rain for three and a half years; he prayed again and rain came. Prayers go unanswered because of doubt, unconfessed sin, selfish motives and unforgiveness.

questions.stem:
(a) Give the second account of creation. [11 marks]
(b) What two lessons can be learnt from the story? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: When the Lord God made the earth and heavens there was no plant or herb, for God had not caused it to rain and there was no man to till the ground; a mist watered the ground
2 marks: The Lord God formed man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living being
2 marks: God planted a garden in Eden with every tree pleasant to sight and good for food, the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; a river watered it and divided into four (Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates)
2 marks: He put the man in the garden to till and keep it, and commanded him not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for in the day he ate of it he would die
2 marks: God said it was not good for man to be alone; He formed beasts and birds and brought them to the man, who named them, but no fit helper was found
1 mark: God caused a deep sleep on the man, took one of his ribs and made a woman; the man called her Woman; a man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife and they become one flesh
2 marks: (b) God is the creator and source of life; man is God's special creation and must obey Him
2 marks: (b) Man is a steward who must work and care for the environment; marriage is ordained by God
questions.explanation: In the second account (Genesis 2), before any plant grew or rain fell, the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. He planted a garden in Eden, eastward, with every pleasant and fruitful tree, including the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; a river flowed out and divided into four rivers. God placed man there to till and keep it and forbade him to eat of the tree of knowledge on pain of death. Seeing it was not good for man to be alone, God formed the animals and birds, and Adam named them, but none was a suitable partner. So God put Adam into a deep sleep, took a rib and made a woman, whom Adam welcomed as bone of his bones; hence a man leaves his parents and is joined to his wife. Lessons: God is the creator and giver of life; man must obey God, care for creation and honour marriage.

questions.stem:
