questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law and led it to Horeb, the mountain of God
2 marks: The angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of a bush; the bush burned but was not consumed, and Moses turned aside to see
2 marks: God called 'Moses, Moses' and told him to remove his shoes for he stood on holy ground; He said He was the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and Moses hid his face
2 marks: God said He had seen the affliction of His people in Egypt and had come to deliver them and bring them to a land flowing with milk and honey; He was sending Moses to Pharaoh
1 mark: God revealed His name 'I AM WHO I AM' and gave Moses signs: the rod that became a serpent and the leprous hand
2 marks: (b) 'Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh?' (feeling of unworthiness)
2 marks: (b) 'They will not believe me or listen to my voice'
2 marks: (b) 'I am not eloquent; I am slow of speech and tongue'; also 'send some other person' / not knowing God's name
questions.explanation: While tending Jethro's flock near Horeb, Moses saw a bush burning without being consumed. When he turned aside, God called him from the bush, told him to remove his sandals because the ground was holy, and introduced Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. God said He had seen Israel's suffering in Egypt and would deliver them to a good land flowing with milk and honey, and was sending Moses to Pharaoh to bring them out. God revealed His name, I AM WHO I AM, and gave him signs. Moses raised excuses: who was he to go to Pharaoh; what name of God should he give; the people would not believe him; he was slow of speech; and finally he begged God to send someone else, so God appointed Aaron as his spokesman.

questions.stem:
(a) Give the account of the healing of Naaman. [12 marks]
(b) What three lessons can be derived from the story? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, a great and honoured man, was a leper
2 marks: A little Israelite girl captured in a raid, who served Naaman's wife, said the prophet in Samaria would cure him
2 marks: The king of Syria sent Naaman with a letter and gifts to the king of Israel, who tore his clothes thinking it was a quarrel
2 marks: Elisha asked the king to send Naaman to him; when Naaman came, Elisha sent a messenger telling him to wash seven times in the Jordan
2 marks: Naaman was angry, expecting the prophet to come out and wave his hand, and saying Abana and Pharpar were better rivers; his servants persuaded him
2 marks: He dipped himself seven times in the Jordan and his flesh was restored like a little child's; he returned to Elisha, confessed there is no God but in Israel, and offered gifts, which Elisha refused
1 mark: (b) God's power is universal and heals people of all nations
1 mark: (b) Humility and obedience bring blessing; pride can block it
1 mark: (b) Even a servant/a child can be God's instrument; God's gifts are free
questions.explanation: Naaman, the honoured commander of the Syrian army, was a leper. An Israelite girl serving his wife said the prophet in Samaria could cure him, so the king of Syria sent him with a letter and rich gifts to the king of Israel, who tore his clothes in dismay. Elisha sent for Naaman and, without coming out, told him through a messenger to wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman went away angry, thinking the rivers of Damascus were better, but his servants persuaded him to obey. He dipped seven times and his flesh became like a little child's. He returned to Elisha, declared that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel, and pressed gifts on him, which Elisha refused. Lessons: God's power reaches all nations; humility and obedience bring healing; God can use humble people; His gifts are free.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem:
(a) Highlight the social injustice in Israel during the time of Amos. [11 marks]
(b) In what two ways can social injustice be eradicated in your society? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: They sold the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes
2 marks: They trampled the head of the poor into the dust and turned aside the way of the afflicted
2 marks: A man and his father went in to the same maiden; they lay down on garments taken in pledge and drank wine of those fined in the house of their God
2 marks: The rich women of Samaria ('cows of Bashan') oppressed the poor and crushed the needy; they lived in luxury on beds of ivory
2 marks: Judges took bribes and turned justice to wormwood; they hated those who reproved in the gate and abhorred those who spoke the truth
1 mark: Traders made the ephah small and the shekel great, dealt deceitfully with false balances and sold the refuse of the wheat
2 marks: (b) Enforcing the rule of law and fair, corruption-free judiciary
2 marks: (b) Fair distribution of resources, care for the poor and moral/religious education
questions.explanation: In Amos' time Israel was prosperous but deeply unjust. The righteous were sold for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals; the poor were trampled and the afflicted pushed aside. Father and son lay with the same girl, and people lay beside altars on garments taken in pledge and drank wine bought with fines. The wealthy women of Samaria, the 'cows of Bashan', oppressed the poor, while the rich lived in luxury on ivory beds. Courts were corrupt: judges took bribes, afflicted the righteous and hated those who spoke the truth at the gate. Traders used false measures and sold the chaff of wheat. Social injustice can be removed by upholding the rule of law with an honest judiciary, by fair distribution of wealth and care for the poor, and by moral education.

questions.stem:
(a) Give the account of the temptation of Jesus as recorded in Matthew's Gospel. [9 marks]
(b) State three points of significance in this story. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil; He fasted forty days and forty nights and was hungry
2 marks: The tempter said, 'If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become loaves of bread'; Jesus answered, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God'
2 marks: The devil took Him to the pinnacle of the temple and said, 'Throw yourself down', quoting that angels would bear Him up; Jesus replied, 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God'
2 marks: The devil showed Him all the kingdoms of the world from a very high mountain and offered them if He would fall down and worship him; Jesus said, 'Begone, Satan! You shall worship the Lord your God and Him only shall you serve'
1 mark: Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him
2 marks: (b) Jesus overcame temptation with the word of God, an example for Christians
2 marks: (b) It showed His obedience to God and that He would not misuse His power
2 marks: (b) It prepared Him for His ministry; Christians too will be tempted but can overcome
questions.explanation: After His baptism Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where He fasted forty days and nights and became hungry. The tempter challenged Him, as Son of God, to turn stones into bread; Jesus replied that man does not live by bread alone but by every word from God's mouth. The devil set Him on the pinnacle of the temple and, quoting scripture, urged Him to throw Himself down; Jesus answered that one must not put the Lord God to the test. Finally the devil showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and offered them in exchange for worship; Jesus commanded, 'Begone, Satan,' for God alone is to be worshipped. The devil left and angels ministered to Him. Significance: Jesus defeated Satan with scripture, showed total obedience and refused to misuse His power, and set an example that temptation can be overcome.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) Relate the parable of the Wheat and Tares. [12 marks]
(b) Identify three lessons that can be learnt from the parable. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field
2 marks: While men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds (tares) among the wheat and went away
2 marks: When the plants came up and bore grain, the weeds appeared also; the servants asked the householder where the weeds came from, and he said, 'An enemy has done this'
2 marks: The servants asked whether to gather the weeds, but he said no, lest in gathering them they root up the wheat; both should grow together until the harvest
2 marks: At harvest he would tell the reapers to gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into his barn
2 marks: Explanation: the sower is the Son of man, the field the world, the good seed the sons of the kingdom, the weeds the sons of the evil one, the enemy the devil, the harvest the close of the age and the reapers angels
1 mark: (b) Good and evil people live together in the world until judgement
1 mark: (b) God is patient; judgement belongs to God, not to men
1 mark: (b) At the end the wicked will be punished and the righteous rewarded, so believers should remain faithful
questions.explanation: Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field, but while men slept an enemy sowed tares among the wheat. When the crop grew, the tares appeared. The servants asked whether to pull them up, but the master said no, lest they uproot the wheat with them; both should grow until harvest, when the reapers would gather the tares to be burned and the wheat into the barn. Jesus explained that the sower is the Son of man, the field is the world, the good seed are the children of the kingdom, the tares the children of the evil one, the enemy the devil, the harvest the end of the age and the reapers the angels. Lessons: good and evil coexist until judgement; God is patient and judgement is His; the wicked will be punished and the righteous will shine, so believers must remain faithful.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) Give the account of the mission of the seventy. [11 marks]
(b) Indicate two lessons that can be derived from this mission. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: The Lord appointed seventy others and sent them two by two ahead of Him into every town and place where He was about to come
2 marks: He said the harvest is plentiful but the labourers few, so pray the Lord of the harvest to send labourers; He sent them as lambs among wolves
2 marks: They were to carry no purse, bag or sandals and salute no one on the road; in a house they should say 'Peace be to this house', stay there eating what was provided, for the labourer deserves his wages
2 marks: They were to heal the sick and say 'The kingdom of God has come near to you'; where not received, they should wipe off the dust of the town as a warning
2 marks: Jesus pronounced woes on Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum; 'He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you rejects me'
1 mark: The seventy returned with joy saying even the demons were subject to them; Jesus said He saw Satan fall like lightning, but they should rejoice that their names were written in heaven
2 marks: (b) Christians must be committed to evangelism and depend on God for provision
2 marks: (b) Teamwork and prayer are needed in God's work; rejoice more in salvation than in power
questions.explanation: Jesus appointed seventy others and sent them in pairs ahead of Him to every town He would visit. He told them the harvest was plentiful but labourers few, so they should pray for more workers; He sent them as lambs among wolves, taking no purse, bag or sandals and not stopping to greet people on the road. Entering a house they were to say 'Peace be to this house', remain there eating what was offered, heal the sick and announce that the kingdom of God had come near. Where they were rejected they should wipe off the town's dust as a sign. He pronounced woes on unrepentant Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum. The seventy returned joyfully, reporting that even demons submitted to them; Jesus said He saw Satan fall like lightning, but they should rather rejoice that their names were written in heaven. Lessons: Christians must be zealous in evangelism, trust God for provision, work together and value salvation above power.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the conversion of the Ethiopian Eunuch. [11 marks]
(b) What two lessons can be learnt from the life of the Eunuch? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: An angel of the Lord told Philip to go south to the road from Jerusalem to Gaza, a desert road
2 marks: There he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a minister of Candace queen of the Ethiopians in charge of her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship and was returning, reading the prophet Isaiah in his chariot
2 marks: The Spirit told Philip to join the chariot; Philip asked, 'Do you understand what you are reading?' and the eunuch said, 'How can I, unless some one guides me?' and invited him up
2 marks: The passage was 'As a sheep led to the slaughter...'; the eunuch asked whom the prophet meant, and beginning with this scripture Philip told him the good news of Jesus
2 marks: At some water the eunuch asked, 'What is to prevent my being baptized?'; they went down into the water and Philip baptized him
1 mark: The Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away and the eunuch went on his way rejoicing
2 marks: (b) Eagerness to study scripture and humility to seek help in understanding it
2 marks: (b) Prompt response to the gospel through faith and baptism; joy follows salvation
questions.explanation: An angel directed Philip to the desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza. There he met an Ethiopian eunuch, treasurer of Queen Candace, returning from worship in Jerusalem and reading Isaiah aloud in his chariot. Prompted by the Spirit, Philip ran up and asked whether he understood what he read. The eunuch admitted he needed a guide and invited Philip to sit with him. He was reading Isaiah 53 about the lamb led to slaughter and asked whom it described; Philip used it to preach Jesus to him. When they came to water the eunuch asked to be baptized; they went down into the water and Philip baptized him. The Spirit then caught Philip away, and the eunuch went home rejoicing. Lessons: we should read God's word eagerly and humbly seek understanding, and respond promptly to the gospel, which brings joy.

questions.stem:
(a) With reference to the book of Galatians, state any six factors that make unbelievers become children of God. [12 marks]
(b) In what three ways can Christians retain their status as children of God? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Faith in Christ Jesus: 'in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith'
2 marks: Baptism into Christ: those baptized into Christ have put on Christ
2 marks: Unity in Christ, in whom there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female
2 marks: Belonging to Christ makes one Abraham's offspring and an heir according to the promise
2 marks: Redemption by the Son, born of woman and under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons
2 marks: Receiving the Spirit of His Son in our hearts, crying 'Abba! Father!'; no longer slaves but sons and heirs
1 mark: (b) Living by the Spirit and bearing the fruit of the Spirit
1 mark: (b) Standing firm in Christian freedom and not returning to bondage/the works of the flesh
1 mark: (b) Loving one another and serving others through love
questions.explanation: Paul told the Galatians that people become children of God through faith in Christ Jesus. In baptism they put on Christ; in Him distinctions of race, status and sex vanish, and all are one. Belonging to Christ makes them Abraham's offspring and heirs of the promise. God sent His Son, born of a woman and under the law, to redeem those under the law so that they might be adopted as sons; and He sent the Spirit of His Son into their hearts crying 'Abba, Father', so they are no longer slaves but sons and heirs. Christians keep this status by walking in the Spirit and bearing its fruit, standing firm in freedom without returning to the works of the flesh, and serving one another in love.

questions.stem:
(a) Highlight Paul's admonition to the Thessalonian Christians concerning the second coming of the Lord. [9 marks]
(b) State three ways Christians can show their adherence to this teaching. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: They should not grieve over those who have died as others who have no hope; God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep
2 marks: The Lord will descend from heaven with a cry of command, the archangel's call and the trumpet of God; the dead in Christ will rise first, then the living will be caught up to meet the Lord in the air
2 marks: The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, when people say 'peace and security'; so they must keep awake and be sober, wearing the breastplate of faith and love and the helmet of hope
2 marks: They should not be quickly shaken or alarmed by claims that the day has come; the rebellion and the man of lawlessness must come first
1 mark: They should comfort one another, stand firm, and not be idle but work quietly
2 marks: (b) Living holy, watchful lives in readiness
2 marks: (b) Encouraging and comforting one another, especially the bereaved
2 marks: (b) Continuing in honest work and avoiding false teachings about the end
questions.explanation: Paul told the Thessalonians not to grieve like those without hope over believers who had died, for as Jesus died and rose, God will bring the departed with Him. The Lord Himself will descend with a command, the archangel's call and the trumpet of God; the dead in Christ will rise first, and those alive will be caught up with them to meet the Lord in the air and be with Him for ever. The day will come like a thief in the night, so they must stay awake and sober, armed with faith, love and hope. In his second letter he warned them not to be alarmed by claims that the day had already come, because the rebellion and the man of lawlessness must appear first, and he told them to stand firm and work quietly. Christians show adherence by watchful, holy living, comforting one another and continuing in diligent work while rejecting false predictions.

questions.stem:
(a) Highlight James' teaching on prayers. [12 marks]
(b) What three factors make prayers ineffective? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Anyone lacking wisdom should ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach
2 marks: One must ask in faith, without doubting; the doubter is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind and is double-minded
2 marks: People do not receive because they do not ask, or they ask wrongly, to spend it on their passions
2 marks: The suffering should pray and the cheerful should sing praise; the sick should call the elders to pray over them, anointing with oil in the Lord's name
2 marks: The prayer of faith will save the sick and the Lord will raise him up; sins will be forgiven; confess sins to one another and pray for one another
2 marks: The prayer of a righteous man has great power; Elijah prayed and it did not rain for three years and six months, and prayed again and rain came
1 mark: (b) Doubt/lack of faith
1 mark: (b) Wrong/selfish motives
1 mark: (b) Unconfessed sin/unrighteous living
questions.explanation: James taught that whoever lacks wisdom should ask God, who gives generously, but must ask in faith without doubting, for a doubter is unstable like a wave tossed by the wind and should not expect anything. People lack things because they do not ask, or because they ask with wrong motives to satisfy their passions. Those suffering should pray, the cheerful sing praises, and the sick call the elders to pray over them and anoint them with oil; the prayer of faith will heal and sins will be forgiven. Believers should confess sins to one another and pray for one another, for the prayer of a righteous man is powerful, as shown by Elijah, whose prayers stopped and then brought rain. Prayers fail through doubt, selfish motives and unconfessed sin.

questions.stem:
(a) What was Peter's advice to Christians undergoing persecution? [11 marks]
(b) Mention two areas in which Christians are persecuted in the society. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: They should rejoice even though they suffer various trials, for the genuineness of their faith, more precious than gold, is tested by fire
2 marks: If they suffer for righteousness' sake they are blessed; they should not fear but reverence Christ as Lord and always be ready to give a defence of their hope with gentleness
2 marks: Keep a clear conscience so that those who abuse their good behaviour may be put to shame; it is better to suffer for doing right than for doing wrong
2 marks: Christ also suffered for sins once for all, leaving an example; they should arm themselves with the same thought
2 marks: Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal; rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings; if reproached for the name of Christ they are blessed; none should suffer as a murderer or wrongdoer
1 mark: Those who suffer according to God's will should entrust their souls to a faithful Creator and do right; God will restore, establish and strengthen them
2 marks: (b) At the workplace (denial of promotion, mockery for refusing bribes or immoral demands)
2 marks: (b) In the family/community or in politics and schools (rejection by relatives, religious violence, discrimination)
questions.explanation: Peter encouraged suffering Christians to rejoice, because trials test and purify their faith like gold in fire and lead to praise when Christ is revealed. If they suffer for righteousness they are blessed; they should not fear their persecutors but honour Christ as Lord, always ready to explain their hope with gentleness and respect, keeping a clear conscience so that slanderers are put to shame. It is better to suffer for doing good than for doing evil, following the example of Christ, who suffered once for sins. They should not be surprised by fiery trials but rejoice to share Christ's sufferings, never suffering as criminals, and should entrust themselves to their faithful Creator while doing good. Christians face persecution at work, in families and communities, and in schools and public life.

questions.explanation: After the tenth plague Pharaoh released Israel, and they journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, carrying Joseph's bones. God led them not by the short road through Philistine territory but by the wilderness towards the Red Sea, going before them in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night. At God's command they camped by the sea, and Pharaoh, regretting their release, pursued them with his chariots. The terrified people complained, but Moses told them to stand firm and see the Lord's salvation. The angel of God and the cloud moved behind Israel to separate them from the Egyptians. Moses stretched out his hand, an east wind divided the waters, and Israel crossed on dry ground; when the Egyptians followed, the sea returned and drowned them. Christians enjoy God's presence and power through prayer, obedience, faith and worship.

questions.stem:

questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Solomon assembled the elders and heads of the tribes of Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the covenant from the city of David

2 marks: He blessed the people again and offered peace offerings; the dedication feast lasted seven days and the people went home joyful
1 mark: (b) It is a place of worship and fellowship with God and fellow believers

1 mark: (b) It administers the sacraments and offers moral guidance and social support
questions.explanation: When the temple was finished, Solomon assembled the elders and leaders of Israel in Jerusalem. The priests carried the ark of the covenant, which held the two stone tablets, into the most holy place beneath the cherubim, while innumerable sacrifices were offered. As the priests came out, a cloud filled the house, for the glory of the Lord filled it. Solomon blessed the people, recalling God's promise to David, then knelt before the altar and prayed that God, whom the heavens cannot contain, would hear prayers offered toward this house, forgive His people when they repented, judge justly, and even hear foreigners who prayed there. He blessed the congregation, offered thousands of peace offerings, and held a seven-day feast, after which the people went home rejoicing. The church is significant as a place of worship and fellowship, of teaching and spiritual growth, and of sacraments, guidance and mutual support.

questions.stem:

2 marks: Israel was oppressed for twenty years by Jabin king of Canaan, whose commander Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron
2 marks: Deborah summoned Barak and conveyed God's command to take ten thousand men to Mount Tabor, promising that God would give Sisera into his hand at the river Kishon
2 marks: When Barak refused to go without her, she went with him, but foretold that the glory would go to a woman; she gave the signal: 'Up! This is the day'
1 mark: The Lord routed Sisera; he fled and was killed by Jael; Israel was delivered and the land had rest
2 marks: (b) Women can be effective leaders when they depend on God

2 marks: (b) Wisdom, fairness and cooperation with others in leadership
questions.explanation: Deborah, a prophetess and the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel, sitting under the palm tree of Deborah in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites came for justice. When Israel had been oppressed for twenty years by Jabin of Hazor and his general Sisera with nine hundred iron chariots, Deborah summoned Barak and told him God's command to gather ten thousand men at Mount Tabor, promising victory at the river Kishon. Barak insisted that she come; she agreed but foretold that a woman would get the glory. She gave the signal for battle, the Lord routed Sisera's army, and Sisera, fleeing on foot, was killed by Jael. Israel was delivered. Women can learn from her that God uses women as leaders, that courage and decisiveness matter in crises, and that a leader should be wise, just and able to work with others.

questions.explanation: Ezra, a priest and scribe learned in the law of Moses, led a party of exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem in the reign of Artaxerxes, who gave him authority, gifts for the temple and power to appoint judges and teach the law. Ezra had set his heart to study, obey and teach God's law. In Jerusalem he learnt that many, including priests and Levites, had married foreign women and adopted their abominations. He tore his clothes, fasted and offered a prayer of confession. The people gathered weeping, confessed their sin and resolved to put away foreign wives, and this was carried out. Ezra also read the law to the people, leading them to renew their covenant with God. Negative attitudes in Christianity today include hypocrisy, materialism and commercialisation of religion, and immorality or disunity among believers.

2 marks: When Mary asked how, Gabriel said the Holy Spirit would come upon her; Mary accepted, 'Let it be to me according to your word'
2 marks: Mary visited her kinswoman Elizabeth, whose babe leaped in her womb; Elizabeth blessed her and Mary sang the Magnificat
2 marks: A decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled, when Quirinius was governor of Syria

2 marks: While there she gave birth to her first-born son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn

1 mark: (b) It teaches humility and brings peace and joy to all people
questions.explanation: Luke records that the angel Gabriel was sent to Nazareth to Mary, a virgin engaged to Joseph of David's house, announcing that she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son, Jesus, the Son of the Most High. Mary humbly accepted. She visited Elizabeth, who was carrying John; the baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb and Mary praised God in the Magnificat. Later Caesar Augustus decreed a census of the whole world while Quirinius governed Syria, so Joseph went with the pregnant Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem, David's city, to be enrolled. There Mary gave birth to her first-born son, wrapped Him in swaddling cloths and laid Him in a manger, since there was no room in the inn. The birth fulfils prophecy about the Messiah, demonstrates God's love in the incarnation, and teaches humility while bringing peace and joy to all.

2 marks: (b) Salvation/eternal life and forgiveness of sins

questions.explanation: After Jesus fed five thousand people with five loaves and two fish, the crowd wanted to make Him king, so He withdrew, and that night walked on the sea to His disciples. The crowd later found Him at Capernaum. He told them they were seeking Him because they had eaten the loaves, and urged them to work for the food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of man gives; the work God requires is to believe in the one He sent. They demanded a sign, recalling the manna Moses gave. Jesus replied that the true bread from heaven is given by His Father and gives life to the world. When they asked for this bread, He declared, 'I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst.' Man's basic spiritual needs include salvation and eternal life, and fellowship with God nourished by His word.

2 marks: If anyone asked, they were to say 'The Lord has need of them'; this fulfilled the prophecy: 'Behold, your king is coming to you, humble, and mounted on an ass'

questions.explanation: Approaching Jerusalem, Jesus reached Bethphage on the Mount of Olives and sent two disciples to the village opposite to untie an ass and her colt, telling them to say, 'The Lord has need of them.' This fulfilled Zechariah's prophecy of the humble king riding on an ass. They brought the animals, laid their garments on them and Jesus sat on them. A great crowd spread their garments on the road, while others cut branches and spread them. The crowds going before and following Him shouted, 'Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!' The whole city was stirred, asking who He was, and the crowds answered that He was the prophet Jesus from Nazareth. Lessons: believers should joyfully honour Christ as King, and they should be steadfast, unlike crowds whose praise soon turned to 'Crucify him'.

questions.explanation: After Pentecost the believers devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread and prayers. They were together and held everything in common, selling property and goods and distributing to anyone in need. Daily they met in the temple and broke bread in their homes with glad and generous hearts, praising God and enjoying the goodwill of the people, and the Lord added to their number. They were of one heart and soul; no one claimed private ownership, so there was no needy person among them, since owners of land or houses sold them and laid the money at the apostles' feet, as Barnabas did. Ananias and Sapphira, who lied about their gift, were struck dead, and when the Hellenist widows were neglected, seven men were appointed to serve. Lessons: care for the needy, live in unity and prayer, and be honest before God.

2 marks: Rulers are not a terror to good conduct but to bad; the ruler is God's servant for your good and an avenger who executes wrath on the wrongdoer

questions.explanation: In Romans 13 Paul taught that everyone should submit to the governing authorities, because all authority comes from God and existing authorities are instituted by Him. Resisting them is resisting God's ordinance and brings judgement. Rulers are a terror not to good conduct but to bad; the ruler is God's servant for the people's good and bears the sword to punish wrongdoers. Christians should therefore obey not only to avoid punishment but also for the sake of conscience. For the same reason they pay taxes, and they must render to all what is due: taxes, revenue, respect and honour, owing nothing except love. A Christian shows responsible citizenship by obeying the law and respecting authority, paying taxes, and participating in civic life through voting, community service and prayer for leaders.

2 marks: He appeared to James, then to all the apostles, and last of all to Paul himself, as to one untimely born

2 marks: Those who have fallen asleep in Christ would have perished, and Christians would be of all men most to be pitied
2 marks: But Christ has been raised, the first fruits of those who have fallen asleep; as in Adam all die, so in Christ shall all be made alive

questions.explanation: Paul reminded the Corinthians of the gospel he had received: Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, was buried, and was raised on the third day. He then cited witnesses: Christ appeared to Cephas, then the twelve, then to over five hundred brethren at once, most still alive, then to James and all the apostles, and finally to Paul himself. He argued that if the dead are not raised, Christ is not raised; then apostolic preaching and Christian faith are futile, believers are still in their sins, the dead in Christ have perished, and Christians are the most pitiable of people. But Christ has indeed been raised as the first fruits; as all die in Adam, all will be made alive in Christ. The resurrection assures Christians of forgiveness, gives hope of eternal life, and proves Christ's victory over death.

2 marks: Put to death what is earthly in you: immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire and covetousness, which is idolatry
2 marks: Put away anger, wrath, malice, slander and foul talk; do not lie to one another, having put off the old nature with its practices
2 marks: Put on the new nature, renewed in knowledge after the image of its creator, where there is neither Greek nor Jew, slave nor free, but Christ is all
2 marks: Put on compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness and patience, forbearing and forgiving one another, and above all love
2 marks: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts and the word of Christ dwell in you richly; whatever you do, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks
1 mark: (b) Avoiding immorality, lying and other vices
1 mark: (b) Showing love, forgiveness and kindness to others

questions.explanation: Paul taught that believers, raised with Christ, must seek and set their minds on heavenly things. They must put to death earthly vices such as immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire and covetousness, and put away anger, malice, slander, foul talk and lying, having stripped off the old self. They have put on the new self, being renewed in the image of the Creator, in which racial and social distinctions disappear. They should clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, meekness and patience, forgive one another as the Lord forgave them, and above all put on love. Christ's peace should rule their hearts, His word dwell in them richly, and everything be done in the Lord's name with thanksgiving. Christians show this by shunning vice, showing love and forgiveness, and living peaceful, thankful lives for God's glory.

(b) In what three ways can a Christian exhibit his faith. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: What does it profit if a man says he has faith but has not works? Can his faith save him?
2 marks: If a brother or sister is ill-clad and lacks daily food and one says 'Go in peace, be warmed and filled' without giving them their needs, it profits nothing
2 marks: Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead; 'I by my works will show you my faith'
2 marks: Believing that God is one is good, but even the demons believe and shudder
2 marks: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith was active along with his works and completed by them; he was called the friend of God
2 marks: Rahab the harlot was justified by works when she received the messengers; as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so faith apart from works is dead
1 mark: (b) Helping the poor and needy
1 mark: (b) Obeying God's word (being doers, not hearers only)
1 mark: (b) Living a holy life and showing no partiality
questions.explanation: James taught that faith which produces no deeds cannot save. If a believer sees a brother or sister without clothes or food and merely wishes them well, that faith is useless and dead. True faith is shown by works. Mere intellectual belief is not enough, since even demons believe in one God and tremble. Abraham's faith was active with his works and made complete when he offered Isaac, and he was called God's friend; Rahab was justified by works when she sheltered the spies and sent them out another way. So a person is justified by works and not by faith alone; as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead. A Christian shows faith by helping the needy, obeying God's word and living a holy, impartial life.

questions.topic: God, the Controller of the universe
questions.stem: What was the sign of the Covenant between God and Abraham?
questions.explanation: 'You shall be circumcised... and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you' (Gen. 17:11).

questions.stem: Moses learnt from the burning bush experience that God
options: would appoint Aaron to lead His people.
was aware of His people's plight.
questions.explanation: 'I have seen the affliction of my people... I know their sufferings' (Exod. 3:7).

questions.stem: Hophni and Phinehas were regarded as worthless men because of all the following except
options: taking part of raw meat before it was boiled.
treating the offerings of the Lord with contempt.
being aggressive in demanding their portion of sacrifice.
always collecting boiled meat rather than raw.
questions.explanation: Eli's sons demanded raw meat before the fat was burnt, not boiled meat (1 Sam. 2:15).

questions.topic: David's submission to the will of God
questions.stem: Which of the following actions showed that King David was a man after God's own heart?
options: Laid ambush against Saul in the wilderness of Ziph
Secretly sent spies to Saul's camp
Ordered Abishai to slay Saul in his sleep
Rejected the suggestion to slay Saul
questions.explanation: David refused to let Abishai kill Saul, the Lord's anointed (1 Sam. 26:9-11).

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: In his latter days, Solomon destroyed his peaceful reign by
questions.explanation: Solomon's foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, and God raised up adversaries against him (1 Kings 11).

questions.stem: Which of the following actions was taken by King Asa?
options: Confirmation of his mother as queen
questions.explanation: Asa expelled the male cult prostitutes and removed his mother as queen mother, 'but the high places were not taken away' (1 Kings 15:12-14).

questions.stem: Elijah went to the brook Cherith in order to
options: drink from it during the drought.
get water for the prophets of God.
questions.explanation: 'You shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there' (1 Kings 17:4).

questions.stem: Elijah called for a contest between himself and the worshippers of Baal to
options: show that God always answer him by fire.
prove that the drought came from God.
show that he could bring rain.
questions.explanation: The contest was to show whether the Lord or Baal was God (1 Kings 18:21-24).

questions.stem: By seizing Naboth's vineyard Ahab was guilty of
questions.explanation: Elijah said, 'Have you killed, and also taken possession?' (1 Kings 21:19).

questions.stem: Which of the following tribes made life difficult for the Israelites during the time of Gideon?
questions.explanation: The hand of Midian prevailed over Israel for seven years in Gideon's time (Judges 6).

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem: According to Amos' prophecy, the Day of the Lord to the Israelites would be a day of
questions.explanation: 'Is not the day of the Lord darkness, and not light, and gloom with no brightness in it?' (Amos 5:18-20).

questions.stem: In Hosea's message, Israel was represented as a
questions.explanation: Hosea's unfaithful wife Gomer symbolised Israel playing the harlot with other gods (Hos. 1-3).

questions.stem: The king of Nineveh ordered his people to fast and pray so that God would
options: make them victorious over their enemies.
remove the punishment meant for them.
avert the series of drought imposed on them.
questions.explanation: 'Who knows, God may yet repent and turn from his fierce anger, so that we perish not?' (Jonah 3:9).

questions.stem: The concept of the new covenant was proclaimed by
questions.explanation: Jeremiah proclaimed the new covenant written on the heart (Jer. 31:31-34).

questions.stem: Isaiah requested the people of Israel to come to the Lord with
questions.explanation: 'Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean... seek justice, correct oppression; defend the fatherless' (Isa. 1:16-17).

questions.stem: The central message of Ezekiel deals with
questions.explanation: Ezekiel taught 'the soul that sins shall die'; each person is responsible for his own sin (Ezek. 18).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: According to the Mosaic law, the only authority to declare a leper healed or cleansed was the
questions.explanation: The law required the leper to show himself to the priest to be pronounced clean (Lev. 13-14).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Which of the following is a nature miracle? The
options: curing the blind man at Jericho.
questions.explanation: The stilling of the storm shows Jesus' power over nature; the others are exorcism, healing and raising the dead.

questions.stem: The parable of the Good Samaritan described the Samaritan as being good mainly because he
options: treated the wounds of the man he met.
conveyed the man to an inn for further attention.
came back to pay for all expenses incurred on the man.
questions.explanation: All his actions flowed from compassion; Jesus' point is 'the one who showed mercy on him' (Luke 10:33-37).

questions.stem: Who among the apostles denied Jesus during his trial?
questions.explanation: Peter denied Jesus three times in the high priest's courtyard.

questions.stem: Jesus was tried before
options: Pilate, Herod and the High Priests.
questions.explanation: Jesus was tried before the high priests (Annas and Caiaphas) and the council, then Pilate and Herod.

questions.stem: Jesus' answer to the question on payment of taxes implies that Christians
questions.explanation: 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's' (Mark 12:17).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Apart from the miracle of the wedding feast, another miracle of Jesus at Cana in Galilee was
questions.explanation: At Cana Jesus told the official his son would live; it was His second sign in Galilee (John 4:46-54).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Jesus described Himself as "the Door" because he
options: enters the sheepfold through a door.
is an open door to everybody.
is the only way to salvation.
laid down his life for his sheep.
questions.explanation: 'I am the door; if any one enters by me, he will be saved' (John 10:9).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: The greatest virtue according to Jesus is
questions.explanation: Jesus named love of God and neighbour as the greatest commandments (Matt. 22:37-40).

questions.stem: On the day of Pentecost, the apostles
questions.explanation: They were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues (Acts 2:4).

questions.stem: What impact did Peter's speech make on the people on Pentecost day?
options: They were so angry that they stoned him
They reported him to the Sanhedrin
He was insulted by the people
questions.explanation: About three thousand souls were added that day (Acts 2:41).

questions.stem: King Herod joined in the persecution of the Church by
options: arresting Paul and threatening to kill him.
killing James the brother of John.
executing the guards who made Peter escaped.
questions.explanation: Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword (Acts 12:2).

questions.stem: The first place that Paul and Barnabas visited during their first missionary journey was
questions.explanation: Sent out from Antioch, they went down to Seleucia, sailed to Cyprus and preached first at Salamis (Acts 13:4-5).

questions.stem: The first Christian Council meeting in Jerusalem was chaired by
questions.explanation: James gave the concluding judgement at the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15:13-21).

questions.stem: In Romans, Christians are encouraged to be subject to Civil Authorities "for the sake of
questions.explanation: 'One must be subject, not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience' (Rom. 13:5).

questions.stem: In the epistle to the Colossians, the task of uplifting the family was assigned to
options: the first son as the heir of the father.
the mother as second in command.
the children as assistants to their parents.
all members of an ideal home.
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:18-21 gives duties to wives, husbands, children and fathers alike.

questions.stem: Paul taught the Galatians that, being a child of God involves
options: paying attention to the elemental spirits.
the indwelling of the spirit of God.
questions.explanation: Because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts (Gal. 4:6).

questions.stem: In Philippians the reward Jesus received for humbling Himself was
options: exaltation as Lord of heaven and earth.
His elevation to the status of servant of God.
questions.explanation: 'Therefore God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name which is above every name' (Phil. 2:9).

questions.stem: Paul in his Epistle, accorded praise to the Philippians because they
options: made regular sacrifices to the Church.
believed more in receiving than in giving.
questions.explanation: He thanked them for the gifts from Epaphroditus, 'a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable to God' (Phil. 4:18).

questions.stem: Paul asked the Thessalonians to imitate his habit of
questions.explanation: Paul worked night and day so as not to burden anyone, to give them an example to imitate (2 Thess. 3:7-9).

questions.stem: Which of the following will precede the resurrection of "the dead in Christ" at Jesus' Second Coming?
options: Cry of command from the Lord
questions.explanation: The Lord will descend with a cry of command... and the dead in Christ will rise first (1 Thess. 4:16).

questions.stem: Through faith in Jesus Christ, Christians become
questions.explanation: 'In Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith' (Gal. 3:26).

questions.stem: According to Paul, God sent His son into the world that both Jews and Gentiles might become children of God through
questions.explanation: God sent His Son so that we might receive adoption as sons (Gal. 4:5).

questions.stem: According to James, "if you do not commit adultery, but do kill, you have
options: become a trangressor of the law.
questions.explanation: 'If you do not commit adultery but do kill, you have become a transgressor of the law' (James 2:11).
